target_customer: Retail crypto traders and investors, mainly in India, who pay trading and product fees
problem: Crypto traders had to code or manually manage strategies across exchanges. Mudrex first offered no-code automated strategies, then pivoted to an Indian crypto investing app.
business_model: transaction fees on crypto trading and investing products (spot, futures, coin sets)

founders.name: Edul Patel
previous_startups: Niffler (SAIF Partners funded, later acquired by Tapzo)
founders.background_notes: e27 (2019) names him as co-founder; education not stated there. YourStory 2019 headline describes the team as IIT alumni but the page returned 403.

founders.name: Alankar Saxena
previous_startups: grocery on credit startup (name not given)

founders.name: Snehil Buxy
founders.background_notes: Named only in the 2019 e27 article; not in the 2022 Entrackr list.

competitors.name: Quantopian
competitors.what: Research platform needing coding for live trading

competitors.name: QuantConnect
competitors.what: Algorithmic trading research platform needing code

competitors.name: FXPro
competitors.what: Visual strategy tool described as very complicated

technical_complexity.rationale: A no-code strategy builder with backtesting and exchange API integrations (Bitmex, Binance) is standard engineering with security and reliability demands.

defensibility.rationale: Trading automation was copyable; later moats were Indian compliance (FIU registration per its site) and user base.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Mudrex paused crypto withdrawals in January 2025 for compliance upgrades and resumed around January 28, 2025.

market_need_then: e27 (2019) reports the founders spoke to about 1,500 traders and 300 registered for the beta, with about 30 percent from India.

branding.brand_signature: Coin Sets, theme based crypto baskets

brand_strength.rationale: Claims 3 million Indian users but no evidence of brand driven growth; only a trademark filing (Feb 2023) found.

pivots.from: Crypto exchange (halted after India central bank ban in April 2018)
pivots.to: No-code automated trading platform, later an investing platform
pivots.why: The RBI banking ban stopped the exchange launch (crypto.news and app developer coverage via search)

outcome_analysis: Mudrex pivoted from an exchange blocked by India's 2018 banking restriction to automated trading in 2019, then to a crypto investing app, raising a 2.5M seed in 2021 and 6.5M in 2022 and claiming over 3 million users. It survived the crypto winter and a January 2025 withdrawal pause tied to compliance work.
notes: The e27 article has no visible date; March 2019 comes from its URL slug. YC page lists only Edul Patel as founder; e27 and Entrackr name the others. Snehil Buxy appears only in the 2019 article. Founder education not found in opened sources (YourStory page returned 403). Round labelled pre-Series A by sources, recorded as other. Total raised not stated by sources opened. Pivot reasoning from search snippets of crypto.news and App Developer Magazine, not opened.
